chunks: And Mismaʿ Kardīn narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning four men who testified against a man for zina, and he was stoned, then one of them retracted and said, “I doubted my testimony.” He عليه السلام said, “The blood money is upon him.”
He said: I said, “What if he said: ‘I testified against him deliberately’?” He عليه السلام said, “He is to be executed.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money due as financial liability
key_terms.الزِّنَا: illicit sexual intercourse that formed the subject of the testimony
key_terms.شَكَكْتُ: I had doubt regarding the truth of what I testified to
key_terms.فَرُجِمَ: he was stoned as the carried-out punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a witness retracts testimony after a person was stoned for zina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a witness who retracts testimony after a hadd punishment has been carried out. If the witness claims doubt, he is liable for blood money; if he admits intentional false testimony, he is subject to execution.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3305 - And it was narrated by Misma' Kardin from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding four witnesses who testified against a man for adultery, and he was stoned. Then one of them retracted and said: "I doubted my testimony."
Imam (as) said: "He must pay the blood money."

I said: What if he said: "I testified against him intentionally"?
Imam (as) said: "He is to be executed."
